steps.text: 13 Years Ago
8:09 P.M. \ Heavy snow
Victoria Border Autonomous Region, County of Toron, Vincent Manor

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: What a splendid blizzard eve! Ladies and gentlemen, welcome, welcome, please come in. Allow the servants to brush the snow off your tops, and thaw yourselves by the brazier.

steps.name: Finely-Dressed Merchant
steps.text: A good evening to you, Count. Truly a magnificent soirée, this is.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Welcome, welcome, Lady Diana. To meet you on the eve of the New Year is my honor entirely.

steps.name: Finely-Dressed Merchant
steps.text: Nonsense. Now take a look, Count. I've a present for you, all the way from Kazimierz.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: What a beautiful pendant! My greatest thanks, Lady Diana, and send my well-wishes to your husband. Now, hurry along inside, we can't have the snow burying your gorgeous looks.

steps.name: Finely-Dressed Merchant
steps.text: Hah! You speak as fine a line as ever.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Oh-ho, look who's here! If it isn't our 'Baron of Rye!'

steps.name: Courteous Nobleman
steps.text: I could never shoulder a title as hefty as Baron, but here I am anyway, the pure nerve!

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: See what you're saying! We all respect you from the bottom of our hearts. Who spurns the man who feeds his people well, now? Ha ha ha!

steps.name: Courteous Nobleman
steps.text: Ah, you're quite right. Once harvest comes next year, I'd be honored if you visit my humble home. The tallest windmills in Toron, the scent of flour everywhere. A stay sure to enchant you, if I do say so myself.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Quite good! This blizzard shall pass, and next year will come trotting in right behind it with fine, fine harvests.

steps.name: Courteous Nobleman
steps.text: My gratitude for your kind words.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Head in and warm yourself up, now. We're serving the spiced bread you so love tonight—of course, baked with most exquisite, fragrant flour, all sourced from your farms.

steps.name: Courteous Nobleman
steps.text: How about you? Won't you come in? It's almost time... Let your good servants welcome the remaining guests.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Perhaps you speak sense, but no matter. I like to greet my invitees personally. They're all the most adorable people, whether noble or merchant, cleric or soldier.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Toron is a fine, fine place, isn't it?

steps.name: Courteous Nobleman
steps.text: Why, you character, you...

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Now, let me see, we still have the Mister and Misses Arizona, that admirable lighthouse operator, and... hm?

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: E-hem.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: I'd heard from my most venerable fellow student, that gifted orator Thomson, that he had recently taken ill, and I couldn't brook the thought of him facing a blizzard for a banquet. Hence my specifically sending for a Messenger, to send him my well-wishes—

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: And yet, imagine my surprise to see—what seems to be a sneaky darling of a Messenger right here!

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Here-here!
Eek!

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Ah-ha, Mistress Heidi, how long since we last met?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Uncle Vincent, don't ruffle up my hair! I had to spend so long making it!

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Fine, fine. Ah, little Heidi, you've grown so much. What a dashing lady you are now.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: However! Your father never sent word you'd be arriving today. Be candid with your uncle now, have you come on the sly?

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: And I say, you're still quite young. If your father saw your dress tonight, you'd be in for the nag, wouldn't you?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Uncle! I'd hate him nagging at me. That's why I slipped off in the first place!

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I heard you called out a gallery of VIPs and bright minds tonight, and I couldn't help my curiosity. Not to mention, my papa always wants me to broaden my scope, get out beyond the classroom, and isn't this the finest opportunity!

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: And you swear you're not here to see the boys, hoping for a chance meeting? You know, your father's told me, you've been absorbed in all those tawdry romance novels lately, and it's been worrying him so.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: How—How—How could I? I'm not such a naive girl now, ah ha ha, ha ha.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Your father worded it very well. Romanticism is all and well, but writing aiming to be consumed, pulling wool over the truths of life, so as to curry favor with readers and wring the last drop of worth from its material; there's nothing of value in it.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: In that regard, all of Toron ought to be learning from your father.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Ahem, Uncle, let's drop the subject now. I feel embarrassed hearing this...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: And honestly, my papa. Telling people off left and right when he was young, and in the end he made himself a businessman, made himself a huge fortune... The old guard in the association constantly joke about him. It drives me mad.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Some things up Life's sleeve you just can't refuse. Oh, well, imagine Thomson did it for you two ladies. Back when he was younger, he'd find any chance to grumble about his unrecognized talent to me. How's his health been lately?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Just his chronic pains. Once winter's gone, he'll be live and well as ever.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: So you availed yourself while your parents couldn't watch you, made off with your mother's clothes, and came to join the festivities?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Right—ah, no, I came on educational purposes, just as my father guided me.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Heidi...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Heh heh. How about you just never saw me?

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: You've been quite too headstrong this time. Look at this awful snow today. Just suppose something had happened to you on the way, how would I ever explain to your father?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Ha, ha ha... well! Uncle, you see, it's so late now anyway. I can't just find a car and head back now, can I?

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Oh, dear, child. Quick, in. Don't you freeze now.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Hooray! You're the best, Uncle!

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Er... but who are you still waiting for? Is there still some guest noble enough to wait like a snowman at the door?

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Quite. An outstanding Laterano cleric.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Last year, your aunt caught some illness unawares, had a fever that wouldn't abate, and it's thanks to that cleric that it vanished.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: We struck up concord afterwards, and I paid frequent visits. This cleric's not just fine with medicine, but has original views on all walks of life. Truly a mind-opener.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Huh... Well, if you vouch for them like this, they must be really incredible, right?

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: But of course. If a person of those talents could swear loyalty to the Vincent family, it'd bring a deal of vigor to building the local land.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: I even had every intent to invite that cleric along as a friend on my journey to Londinium, and your aunt would've appreciated the diversion, but would you know our rotten luck? Out on business.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: So today, mark my words, I'll be introducing this insightful scholar to one and all.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Uncle... is that Laterano cleric—a gentleman by any chance? A refined, mannerly Sankta, maybe? On the older side, or?

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: There it is, you little scamp! Swearing your pure intentions, even!

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Just asking!

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Don't get too excited. She's a meritorious woman. And she isn't a Sankta. Very rare to see, but all suggests she's a Feline cleric. I truly do appreciate people like her.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Ahem...!

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: U—Uncle, I didn't hear any of that, and I won't breathe a word to Auntie, you can cross my heart.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: And what silly ideas have you gotten! I really ought to make Thomson give you a proper word or three!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: My apologies, Sir Vincent.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Might I have arrived late?
